title: Built from scratch in India, for the physical world.
standfirst: ZenteiQ grew out of scientific computing research at IISc. It trained its Dhīr foundation models from scratch on TPUs in India, and on 3 November 2026, MeitY and the IndiaAI Mission released the first two. The company is building AI for engineering, industry and private deployment.

hero.alt: Diagram of Dhīr 5B MoE: a token passes to a router, which sends it to two of twelve expert networks, E01 and E07; the other ten experts are inactive for that token
hero.caption: Inside Dhīr 5B MoE. Each token is routed to two of twelve experts. Illustration adapted from ZenteiQ Research’s training blog (3 November 2026).

lead: General-purpose AI can explain how an aircraft wing or a cooling system works. Engineering teams need something more: predictions checked against measurements, governing equations and proven simulation tools.

ZenteiQ is working towards that by building foundation models, scientific machine learning and applications as one connected technology stack. In November 2026 its first two models, Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B, were released under the IndiaAI Mission.

blocks: ZenteiQ’s founder, Prof. Dr. Sashikumaar Ganesan, is a professor in the Department of Computational and Data Sciences at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, where he leads the AI for Research and Engineering eXcellence (AiREX) Lab. His work spans scientific machine learning, numerical analysis, high-performance computing and hardware-aware numerical methods, and he is a co-author of _Finite Elements: Theory and Algorithms_.

ZenteiQ began in 2022 as an experiment in applying AI to higher education. It later turned to AI for science and engineering R&D. Its long-term aim, in the company’s words, is Scientific Intelligence: AI that supports the analysis and design of physical systems, with rigorous validation kept in the loop.

ZenteiQ trained its released Dhīr models from random initialisation on Google Cloud TPU v6e in India. Every stage ran on TPUs: pretraining, mid-training, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. The company used its own tokenizer, data pipeline, training recipe and evaluation tools, and its published infrastructure includes 2,048 TPU v6e chips in production. ZenteiQ says it was the first company in India to pretrain billion-parameter generative foundation models from scratch on TPUs.

**Dhīr 2B** is a compact dense model with 2.03 billion parameters. **Dhīr 5B MoE** has 5.09 billion parameters, but activates about 1.79 billion for each token by routing it to two of twelve expert networks. Each model was pretrained on more than six trillion tokens, with English and ten Indian languages built in from the start.
Both are designed for private use that can run offline, on laptops and edge devices. ZenteiQ also publishes training provenance and open evaluation tools, so that its key claims can be tested.

On 18 September 2025, at a pre-event of the IndiaAI Summit in Delhi, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced ZenteiQ’s selection under the IndiaAI Mission of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), to build India’s Scientific Foundation Model. The first year carried ₹75 crore, mostly for compute. The plan reported at the time was an 8-billion-parameter model, trained within 12 months.

“We are proud to share that ZenteiQ.ai has been selected to build India’s Scientific Foundation Model (SFM), a vital step towards strengthening the country’s sovereign AI capabilities,” Ganesan wrote on LinkedIn.

On 3 November 2026, MeitY and the IndiaAI Mission formally released Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B at an event in New Delhi attended by MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan. The model files were published on AIKosh, IndiaAI’s national AI platform, and on Hugging Face on 13 November 2026, under the Apache 2.0 licence. ZenteiQ presents them as a case for indigenous AI that can run securely inside an organisation’s own environment, without depending on a constant cloud connection.

panel.title: What ZenteiQ builds
items: Foundation models pretrained from scratch. Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B MoE are released; Dhīr 9B is in development.
Brings scientific machine-learning methods into simulation workflows.
Being piloted for industrial research and development.
Support knowledge and private inference use cases.

blocks: The company is also extending its work towards scientific foundation models and Physical AI. It is careful about where the released models stand: ZenteiQ does not claim that Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B already perform validated engineering reasoning.

sections.h2: ARTPARK and the data behind the models.
blocks: ZenteiQ was incubated at FSID, IISc, and is part of ARTPARK’s startup portfolio. Beyond that, ZenteiQ describes joint work with ARTPARK on the pipelines that prepare scientific and engineering data for model training, and on related engineering platforms.

That work matters because a scientific model is only as dependable as the quality, provenance and reproducibility of the data and computation behind it. The collaboration connects research rooted at IISc with the practical infrastructure needed to scale scientific AI built in India.
The company’s education years also left a trace at ARTPARK. Its Academy lists ARTPARK x Zenteiq AI-Tech Innovations among its industry collaborations, for AI-MPOWER, a programme for educators.
